links.kind: Prospective replay of 13 historical records; historical results were already seen.

question: Do the 13 historical closure certificates reproduce byte-for-byte and pass the independent checker, with retained archive bytes?

claims.text: Each accepted certificate establishes 1 not in W4 and its stated codimension lower bound on exactly the recorded input.

arms.description: Historical exact input replay; independent checker uses separate arithmetic.
Read-only historical certificates.txt digests; no new execution attributed to this arm.

aa.not_applicable_reason: Exact replay compares each complete certificate SHA256 with the historical digest; no stochastic timing claim.

positive.not_applicable_reason: All 13 historical accepted certificates are positive correctness controls; every one must reproduce and independently verify.

negative.not_applicable_reason: Truncation and corruption rejection are software checks, not a statistical null population. No inference from absence of a certificate.

factors.name: input
factors.how: Exact historical parameters and plan hash.

factors.name: instrument
factors.how: C source, M4RI commit and binary SHA256 retained.

factors.name: host
factors.how: CPU, kernel, process memory ceiling and L0 wall-valid=false; no timing inference.

factors.name: order
factors.how: Plan order, two workers; independent exact computations.

comparisons.threshold: Regenerated digest equals historical reference AND independent checker accepts.

randomization.arm_order_reason: Exact named-input replay has no arm-dependent clock inference.

seed_derivation.note: No new random inputs; seed is a run identifier only.

instance_sampling.rule: All 13 certificates in results/certificates.txt, without selection.

blinding.how: Historical outcomes known; no statistical comparison.

power.note: Exhaustive historical list, deterministic verification, no population or power claim.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Conservative scheduling allowance based on historical certificates.txt; old P45a closure ~6000s and check 787s. Not measured on current host.

primary.name: certified codimension lower bound
primary.definition: nq from an independently accepted surjective closure-separating map; not equality with closure codimension.

placement.checkpoint_detail: Completed per-instance results are durable checkpoints; running M4RI state has no checkpoint. Restart interrupted instance into a new attempt, never claim CRIU recovery.

stopping_rules.rule: Attempt the 13 exact historical entries once; infrastructure-only retries are explicit new attempts.
Hash mismatch, checker failure, missing completion or timeout leaves a failed record and retained bytes.

invalidation_rules: Unverified certificate yields no certified lower bound.
No public archive claim until anonymous download and SHA256 readback.

decision_rule.text: Accept each replay only on historical byte identity and independent checker success.
decision_rule.threshold: exact equality and checker exit 0 with explicit VALID marker

outputs: per-instance exact acceptance and retained hashes

graphs: per-instance certificate status, no timing graph

inadmissible: Equating ker(pi) and W4 solely from checker acceptance.
Calling nonmembership alone an unsatisfiability proof.
Claiming an F4 trace establishes an exact LFD.
Claiming a private object store is a public archive.

literature.claim: Prior empirical degree five and distinct first-fall definition.
